name: Unwanted Background Work
problem: Recurring background passes can work when the person's settings say they should not: past the daily budget, on a day outside the roster, or without a cadence being due.
who_has_it: People who set an autopilot cadence and budget for their quest.
why_it_matters: An autopilot that ignores its settings spends money and writes to a quest the person did not ask it to touch, which breaks the promise of the setting.
why_hard: The decision depends on budget, cadence, a pending run-now request, reactive triggers and a roster, and it has to be made before any goal is read or any model is called.
existing_attempts: A cron schedule, a global on or off switch, and per-run checks inside the pass.

name: Work Cut Off From Its Purpose
problem: Replies, experiments and finished work are chosen and judged from the quest alone, not from the top intent and metrics the quest serves, so effort can drift from what the person cares about most and gaps under an intent can go unnoticed.
who_has_it: Anyone with top intents above their quests, and maintainers iterating on a repository's solutions.
why_it_matters: The work done can differ from the work that matters, and the person is not told when an ideal has no solution, a solution has no quest or a metric has no data.
why_hard: The purpose lives in a specification that no prompt used to read, and adding it naively inflates every prompt and charges users who have no intents.
existing_attempts: Life intents specifications, written but read by little that does work; generic standing instructions in deep runs.
